scope: Manual comparison of the 15 remaining interfaces of aos-2024-v52-i04-p1360, preserving the frozen distinctions between iid observations, stationary gapped observations, split chains, cycle-pair data and fresh Gaussian simulation.

rows.query: Stationary dependent sequence and a function of a transformed stationary mean; searched stationary processes and inspected equality of shifted laws, pushforwards, integration and invariant Markov measures.
rows.result: Equality of the process law with each time-shifted law can express stationarity; invariant measures support the Markov-chain specialization once the homogeneous trajectory law is constructed. Integration expresses the scalar mean of g under the stationary marginal.
rows.gap: The setting is composable after specifying a stationary trajectory law and integrable g, without replacing temporal dependence by an iid law.

comparisons.D17: The target is f(E g(X_1)), with g mapping the state space to R and expectation under the stationary measure; stationarity means shift invariance of joint laws, not just identical one-time marginals, and the Markov-chain example is not a restriction that every stationary sequence must satisfy.

rows.query: Vector Cramer characteristic-function condition at norm infinity; searched Cramer and inspected charFun's positive imaginary exponent and filter limsup.
rows.result: The norm of charFun P t has the source's Fourier convention on real Euclidean space, and limsup along the filter where ||t|| tends to infinity gives the displayed numerical condition.
rows.gap: These declarations suffice to state the vector Cramer condition with the correct norm-to-infinity filter.

comparisons.D13: Require limsup_{||t||->infinity}|E_P exp(i<t,X>)|<1 for the raw R^d-valued iid observation law, keeping the positive imaginary exponent and no 2pi factor; neither a one-coordinate limit nor the later cycle or split-process Cramer conditions are the same hypothesis.

rows.query: Finite vector moments through r+2 and nonsingular centered covariance; inspected MemLp, covariance integrals and finite matrix rank.
rows.result: Finite (r+2)-norm moment on a probability space supplies lower moments, and coordinatewise centered covariance yields a square matrix whose full rank expresses nonsingularity. Moment finiteness must be established before totalized covariance integrals are given their statistical interpretation.
rows.gap: These declarations can express the moment and covariance condition with a positive integer r and the centered finite-dimensional covariance matrix.

comparisons.D14: Preserve moments up to order r+2 and nonsingular covariance of the original vector X; the r=2 specialization used by Theorem 6 requires fourth moments, not exponential moments, and covariance must be centered rather than an uncentered second-moment operator.

rows.query: Retained batches separated by n^delta discarded observations and pooled/deleted empirical laws; inspected atomic measures, weighted measure sums, scalar expectation and real powers.
rows.result: Weighted point masses represent each retained batch, and averaging or deleting one batch constructs the other empirical laws. The target functional composes f with the empirical integral of g. The gap length needs integer indexing compatible with the source's real-power notation.
rows.gap: The gapped empirical construction still needs an explicit retained-index and integer-gap convention before reusing the statistic formulas, without claiming exact batch independence.

comparisons.D18: Retain K batches each of n observations after discarding n^delta between adjacent batches for 0<delta<1, form P-hat as their average and P-hat_(i) from the other K-1 batches, and use psi(Pbar)=f(E_Pbar g); require K>1 for deletion and preserve the dependence setting rather than importing the iid law or silently choosing a rounding rule.

rows.query: Harris recurrence as almost-sure infinitely many visits from every starting state; searched Harris recurrence and inspected trajectory laws, frequently_atTop and event probabilities.
rows.result: A Markov trajectory law started at each x and a frequent-visit event express the source quantifiers. No Harris recurrence declaration was located; the printed existential measure can be zero, making its positive-mass-set condition vacuous.
rows.gap: The recurrence predicate can be assembled, but its identification with standard Harris recurrence remains limited by the source's omitted nonzero and sigma-finite measure qualifiers.

comparisons.D20: Keep existence of a measure mu, every measurable B with mu(B)>0, and probability one of infinitely many visits under P_x for every starting x; do not add nonzero or sigma-finite hypotheses to the quotation, and do not reduce infinitely many visits to a single finite hitting time.

rows.query: Strong-mixing coefficient as supremum of event-probability factorization errors over two sigma-fields; searched strong mixing and inspected generated sigma-algebras, event probabilities and bounded real suprema.
rows.result: The two-field coefficient is a bounded supremum of absolute differences of probabilities; comap of past/future observation blocks generates the required sigma-fields. This does not resolve the source's different symbol in its stationary lag formula.
rows.gap: The strong-mixing construction remains to be assembled with whole past/future sigma-fields while preserving the source's unexplained sigma-versus-alpha notation.

comparisons.D19: Use sup_{A in Afield,B in Bfield}|P(A intersect B)-P(A)P(B)|, and preserve the stationary past through time zero and future from n; the final source formula prints sigma(F_-infinity^0,F_n^infinity), not the alpha just defined, so an intended identification must be noted rather than presented as a literal verified equality.

rows.query: Statistical functional given by a real function of a vector mean; inspected Bochner integration of finite-dimensional real vectors.
rows.result: Vector integration followed by f directly gives the functional on distributions with an integrable identity random vector; totalized integrals outside that domain do not automatically represent a mean.
rows.gap: The existing vector integral and function composition suffice on the intended finite-first-moment domain.

comparisons.D12: For a distribution Pbar on R^d, define psi(Pbar)=f(E_Pbar X) with a vector expectation and scalar output; no derivative order, nonzero gradient, independence assumption or scalar g transformation is built into this definition itself.

rows.query: Local r+1-fold differentiability with a nonzero gradient, without continuous highest derivative or normalized first coordinate; inspected pointwise Frechet differentiability and iterated derivative operators.
rows.result: Differentiability of successive derivative maps at each point of a neighborhood can state the finite differentiability order, while nonzero first derivative is equivalent to nonzero Euclidean gradient. Merely having totalized iterated derivatives does not establish their existence.
rows.gap: These declarations can state the local derivative condition once successive derivative existence and the Euclidean gradient identification are supplied.

comparisons.D15: Retain r+1 derivatives in a neighborhood of E_P X and nonzero full gradient at that mean; do not strengthen the text to continuous differentiability of the highest order or require the first partial derivative to be nonzero or equal to one.

rows.query: Symmetric coverage expansion coefficient multiplying n^-1 with n^-3/2 remainder; inspected event probabilities, asymptotic norm bounds and real powers.
rows.result: The residual between the statistic's coverage, its Student reference coverage and c/n can be compared to n^(-3/2) using IsBigO as n tends to infinity. This expresses the target coefficient without producing its simulation estimator.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to state the coverage expansion once the chosen statistic, Student reference law and fixed parameters are supplied.

comparisons.D24: Keep the symmetric event -q<=W<=q, reference t_{K-1} coverage, method-specific c n^-1 and O(n^-3/2), with c allowed to depend on method,K,P,f,q but not n; c is a coverage-expansion coefficient, not the bias of a batch point estimate or a common constant across all four methods.

rows.query: Uniform scalar Edgeworth expansion with alternating polynomial parity and Gaussian CDF/density; searched Edgeworth and inspected normal law, density, CDF and explicit-constant asymptotic bounds.
rows.result: The standard normal CDF/density and finite power corrections are available. A common remainder bound over all q requires an explicit constant and eventual sample threshold uniform in q, not separate pointwise Big-O statements. No Edgeworth-expansion package was located in the searched revision.
rows.gap: The expansion predicate still needs its polynomial corrections, alternating parity and uniform remainder assembled; the existing Gaussian and asymptotic operations do not prove its validity.

comparisons.D16: For positive finite sigma, retain the CDF of sqrt(n)(psi(P-hat_1)-psi)/sigma, corrections sum_{j=1}^r n^(-j/2) p_j(q) phi(q) and uniform O(n^(-(r+1)/2)); p_j is even for odd j and odd for even j, and these scalar correction polynomials must not be identified with the later density-weighted Algorithm 1 expressions bearing the same names.

rows.query: Influence function under continuous Gateaux differentiability and finite positive influence variance; searched Gateaux/influence and inspected directional line derivatives and variance.
rows.result: HasLineDerivAt provides a directional derivative once a vector-space domain and directions are specified, and variance expresses a moment condition for a supplied influence function. Neither determines the paper's unnamed tangent structure or a complete influence-function definition.
rows.gap: The influence-function interface still needs its measure-domain and tangent interpretation specified without replacing the source's Gateaux assumption by a stronger Frechet condition.

comparisons.D29: The main text only names IF of psi at P; Theorem 7 separately supplies continuous Gateaux differentiability and positive finite IF variance, so do not present a particular contamination-path formula, topology, centering condition or stronger differentiability notion as a transcribed definition.

rows.query: Successive recurrent-state return times, cycle reward sums and stationary renewal-reward ratio; searched regenerative cycles and inspected hittingAfter, finite sums and expectations.
rows.result: hittingAfter at initial index one gives the first strictly positive visit, and restarting after T_i+1 gives the next strict return when times are finite; finite interval sums give rewards. The stationary ratio-of-expectations identity requires regenerative and integrability arguments beyond those constructions.
rows.gap: The cycle interface still needs finite successive return times and the regenerative ratio identity justified, with the initial incomplete segment excluded.

comparisons.D22: Take T_1=inf{k>0:X_k=a_0}, T_i the first hit strictly after T_(i-1), and Y_i=sum_{k=T_i}^{T_(i+1)-1}g(X_k); keep the paired reward and duration as observations and E_pi g=E Y_i/E duration, without converting infinite hitting times to ordinary indices, averaging within-cycle ratios or including observations before T_1.

rows.query: Minorized split-chain construction with binary labels, residual transition and regeneration sums; searched split/regeneration infrastructure and inspected Markov kernels, Bernoulli laws, trajectory law and hitting times.
rows.result: A normalized binary product state kernel and its initial law can generate a trajectory. The residual transition requires domination and a valid 1-lambda denominator; generic kernel types and totalized measure subtraction do not establish those properties. Hitting times and sums supply the named derived random quantities.
rows.gap: The split process still needs its piecewise kernel, residual positivity and normalization proved under a valid lambda range before its return time and centered cycle sums have the stated probabilistic meaning.

comparisons.D21: Preserve the recurrent set C and minorization, initial alpha times Bernoulli(lambda), ordinary P transitions outside C, phi_C inside C when b=1 and Q=(P-lambda phi_C)/(1-lambda) inside C when b=0, followed by a fresh binary label; retain tau=min{n>0:X_n in C,b_n=1}, centered g, n^-1/2 partial sums and G through tau, and distinguish binary delta/initial alpha from the gap exponent/mixing coefficient while recording that merely lambda>0 does not settle the residual-kernel domain.

rows.query: Two-dimensional cycle-pair mean ratio and pooled/batched/deleted empirical measures; inspected coordinate expectations and weighted atomic measure constructions.
rows.result: Two coordinate integrals and division define the ratio when the expected duration is positive, and weighted point masses form the empirical substitutions on cycle pairs. The generic CI formulas can then be applied to that functional.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the cycle-pair functional and empirical substitutions on the positive expected-duration domain.

comparisons.D23: Use Q_i=(Y_i,T_(i+1)-T_i) as each of the nK observations and psi(Pbar)=E_Pbar Q^(1)/E_Pbar Q^(2), with pooled, batch and leave-one-batch-out laws of these pairs; this is a ratio of means, not a mean of ratios, and does not apply equal-calendar-time gaps to the variable-length regenerative cycles.

rows.query: Coverage-coefficient simulation initialization with original-law cumulants and fresh correlated Gaussian vectors; inspected iterated derivatives, centered covariance, multivariate Gaussian law, finite products and averages, and searched cumulant-generating infrastructure.
rows.result: The derivatives and centered covariance are representable, and a finite product of N(0,Sigma) laws describes the fresh iid simulation. Low-order original cumulants can be built from mixed moments; an analytic MGF assumption would be stronger than the fourth-moment hypothesis and cannot be inferred here.
rows.gap: The initialization still needs the original-law cumulant tensors and statistic input assembled with the Gaussian simulation, without asserting validity or unbiasedness of the later printed algorithm.

comparisons.D26: Supply f derivatives through order three and original X_1 cumulants through order four, then simulate K new iid Gaussian vectors with mean zero and original centered covariance Sigma, set A_0 to their mean and B_i=X_i-A_0; the reused X_i notation does not assert Gaussian original observations, and centering the fresh draws makes the B_i dependent rather than another iid family.
